newsitem.title: USA: Wells Fargo stolen money believed found -FBI.
newsitem.headline: Wells Fargo stolen money believed found -FBI.

text.p: Federal authorities said on Friday they have recovered $2.4 million in cash that appears to be part of $2.5 million stolen from a Wells Fargo facility in Youngstown, Ohio, on Nov. 29.
The money, $2,445,350 in cash, was found in a storage unit in Boardman, Ohio, a Youngstown suburb, the FBI and the U.S. Attorney for the northern district of Ohio said in a joint news release.
"The money appears to be part of the proceeds of the larceny which occurred at the Wells Fargo Youngstown facility on Nov. 29, 1996, in which $2,550,950 was stolen," they said.

Leesa Mazon, 27, of Struthers, Ohio, who was a Wells Fargo employee, and Jeffery Chicase, 33, of Poland, Ohio, have been indicted by a federal grand jury and charged with conspiracy and bank larceny in connection with the case.

If convicted, Mazon could face up to 15 years in prison and Chicase, who was also charged with receiving stolen property, could face up to 20 years. They also could be fined, U.S. Attorney Emily Sweeney has said.
Wells Fargo armoured services is a unit of Chicago-based Borg-Warner Security Corp.
